title: Rerun M4 retrieval check on canonical-alignment checkpoint
description: Why: the current retrieval report is attached to the pre-overhaul model. After the aligned checkpoint lands, retrieval and its interpretation need to be recomputed on the new representation. What: rebuild the retrieval index on the aligned checkpoint, rerun the entropy gate and baseline contrast on both holdouts, and refresh the per-minute tables used by downstream M4 follow-ups. Acceptance: an updated retrieval report exists for the aligned checkpoint; the index artifact metadata references the new checkpoint/code sha; and downstream M4 diagnostic beads can depend on this rerun instead of the older proxy-era report.

title: Train and evaluate first canonical-alignment world-model checkpoint
description: Why: once the canonical architecture deltas land, the project needs an explicit retrain/eval pass rather than treating retraining as implicit cleanup. What: train a new checkpoint on the current corpus after the canonical-overhaul beads land, then rerun the Plan B-style evaluation suite with game-cold, player-cold, leak-probe, and rollout diagnostics. Acceptance: a new checkpoint and eval report are produced; the report names the canonical inputs/targets used; and any remaining proxy caveats are called out explicitly.

title: Align decoder heads on [h_t || z_t] anchor representation
description: Why: the canonical spec defines r_t = [h_t || z_t] as the shared anchor representation for prediction, while the current implementation still drives decoder heads mostly from z_t alone. What: move the four core decoder heads onto the shared [h_t || z_t] representation and keep retrieval on [h_t || mu_q(z_t)] so training and downstream retrieval finally agree on the anchor contract. Acceptance: next-event, next-observation, outcome, and next-decision heads all consume the shared anchor representation; tests and checkpoints reflect the new dimensional contract.

title: Replace pooled between-anchor summaries with event-token recurrence
description: Why: the canonical spec locks hybrid time and requires event tokens to update the world model between anchors. The current pooled per-minute action_summary remains a temporary proxy. What: advance the recurrent state in true event order within each anchor interval, then apply the anchor posterior update at the observation boundary. Acceptance: event tokens are no longer collapsed to one mean-pooled summary per anchor window; recurrence runs over ordered event tokens; batching/tests cover variable event counts and anchor boundaries.

title: Condition static game context at every model step
description: Why: the canonical world-model spec requires Stream 1 to condition the sequence model at every anchor/event step, not just seed h0. Today Plan B uses static_to_h(static) to initialize the recurrent state and then mostly drops static context. What: represent static game context as per-game tokens (champion/side tokens plus a misc-context token for queue, region, time bucket, patch params, etc.) and add a per-step conditioning path so dynamic updates can attend to static context throughout the sequence. Acceptance: static context is available to every dynamic update step; the implementation no longer treats h0 seeding alone as compliant Stream-1 conditioning; tests cover shape/plumbing and preserve leak discipline.

title: Plan first architecture-alignment retrain from canonical world-model spec
description: Why: the new canonical world-model spec names a set of open questions that must be answered deliberately before the next model-alignment retrain. What: produce an implementation/retraining plan that decides the first full-fidelity anchor observation bundle, the event target factorization, the static conditioning mechanism, the recurrence staging strategy, and whether head inputs move to [h||z] in the same retrain. Acceptance: the follow-up plan references the canonical spec, records decisions for those five questions, and sequences the existing implementation beads so the next retrain scope is explicit.
notes: Delivered docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md, created the missing canonical-alignment beads, and rewired dependencies so the implementation queue now phases through inputs -> recurrence/heads -> rollout -> retrain -> retrieval.

title: Write canonical superpowers model spec
description: Why: the original sequence-model spec captures the strict long-term goals, but downstream Plan A / Plan B / M4 docs introduced milestone proxies and partial gates that are now distributed across several files. What: add a new canonical spec under docs/superpowers/specs that preserves the original draft, reconciles the downstream docs, clearly separates source-of-truth architecture from milestone approximations, and records the open questions raised by the stricter design. Acceptance: a new spec file exists; it does not overwrite the 2026-04-15 sequence-model spec; it explains final architecture vs temporary proxies vs open questions; it is specific enough to guide later code changes and retraining decisions.

title: Expand anchor observations with richer timeline and team-macro features
description: notes/timeline_architecture and notes/clickhouse_array envision a much richer per-timestamp player-state tensor than the current Plan B observation path. Today AnchorObservationProjector only sees 10×6 features (total_gold, xp, level, pos_x, pos_y, cs), while the parser already computes or could derive more signal: current_gold, jungle_cs, kills/deaths/assists, wards/items, objective state, and team-macro features already implemented in code/features.py (gold diff, tower/objective counts, centroid/spread). Follow-up should widen the observation bundle and test whether it improves retrieval quality and downstream lesson sharpness.

title: Make world-model tokens target-aware and subtype-aware
description: The current tokenizer keeps only coarse event type + actor slot. target_slot is dropped in the dataset/model path, and events.details fields such as itemId, skillSlot, monsterType, laneType, towerType, and buildingType are ignored. That means ITEM_PURCHASED cannot distinguish boots from IE, SKILL_LEVEL_UP cannot distinguish Q/W/E/R, and objective events lose crucial semantics. Follow-up should extend tokenization/embeddings/heads so decision and outcome modeling can condition on event subtypes and targets, closer to the actor×target factorization in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-sequence-model-design.md.

title: Fill out static game-context stream beyond patch version scaffolding
description: Current Plan B static stream is effectively patch-version-only: MatchDataset calls patch_vector_for_match() in default scaffolding mode, which yields just the version triple (3 non-zero dims) and omits champion picks, side assignments, queue/region, time-of-day, and first-dragon context. This diverges from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-sequence-model-design.md, which expects a real static game-context stream. Follow-up should add a proper static feature bundle (picks + side + queue/region/time buckets now, richer numeric patch params later) and plumb it through dataset/encoders without reintroducing label leak.

title: Lift train-set self-retrieval: add exclude_match_id to query_index
description:
Today `generate_lesson` refuses to process train-set matches because the M4 retrieval index was built from train games; querying from a train match returns itself as its own top-k neighbour and collapses the cohort.

Fix: parameter-level filter, no index rebuild.

**Changes:**
- `code/model/retrieval.py::query_index` — accept optional `exclude_match_ids: set[str] | None`. Fetch top-`k + buffer` with `buffer = len(exclude) + small_margin`, mask cohort rows whose `bundle.row_match_id` ∈ exclude, trim back to `k`. Default None = current behavior.
- `code/model/lesson.py::generate_lesson` — always pass `exclude_match_ids={match_id}`. Drop the "holdout only" caveat from module docstring.
- `code/tests/model/test_lesson.py` — integration test on a train-set match_id (pick first from plan_a_holdout minus … actually just any `load_split('train')[0]`) asserting cohort doesn't contain target.

**Why not rebuild:** the 800 MB index is checkpoint-bound. Masking is O(k·|exclude|) per query, trivial.

**Acceptance:**
- lesson CLI runs on a train-set match_id and returns cohorts that do not contain the target match_id.
- All existing tests pass.

title: Align docs/superpowers model docs with actual Plan A/Plan B scope and gates
description: The docs/superpowers model draft has drifted in a few important ways that make the current story internally inconsistent. Follow-up should tighten the documentation, not necessarily change code. Issues found during the 2026-04-22 review: (1) core sequence spec says static stream includes picks/sides/queue/region/time-of-day and is cross-attended each anchor, but Plan A/Plan B plans/self-reviews treat patch_params + StaticContextEncoder as covering that scope; (2) core spec says next-event head is categorical over event type × actor × target and event tokens feed RSSM between anchors, but Plan B design/plan quietly relax this to multi-hot 11-class event windows and pooled action summaries; (3) Plan B design says KL weight starts at 0.01 and static encoder is 1024→512→512 cross-attended each step, while the implementation plan uses D_STATIC=512 despite reusing Plan A encoders and maps the KL setting to KL_WEIGHT_LOSS=0.05 with only a hand-wavy equivalence note; (4) M4 retrieval spec uses a one-sided entropy gate (>=0.7) even though the same doc says random cohorts are ~1.0 and bad, so the real success condition is a band/baseline comparison, not a simple threshold; (5) surrounding eval reports should be reconciled with spec gate text where monotonic AUC / rollout ordering were expected but not observed. Deliverable: update the docs so the intended model draft, temporary simplifications, and actual acceptance criteria are explicit and non-contradictory.

title: Design: latent archetypes for lesson-plan personalization (not retrieval)
description:
Scope design pass for archetype work. User constraint: archetypes are **latent, fluid, multi-dimensional** (role, time-of-day, intra-game phase can all shift them) and must NOT be used to filter retrieval cohorts. Cohorts remain action-basis (z_t retrieval). Archetypes feed only the lesson-plan selector — *how* we teach, not *what* we retrieve.

Why this separation:
- Counterfactual signal lives in the state-nearest cohort. Filtering the cohort by archetype throws away the "same situation, different outcome" evidence the whole M4 gate validated.
- Archetype matters for lesson framing + sequencing: a greedy-farm archetype and a greedy-roam archetype may both be "in this state" but the minute-4 advice differs in wording and focus.

Design questions to settle before implementing:
1. **Representation.** Three candidates:
   a. Single continuous embedding per (puuid, session) — lives in latent space, no discrete labels surfaced.
   b. Short-window trajectory fingerprint (last N anchors of h_t) — captures intra-game shifts.
   c. Behaviour-stat vector from crafted features — interpretable, good for "you always X" prose.
   Likely hybrid: (a) for personalization routing, (c) for lesson prose substitutions.
2. **Conditioning signal.** role, time-of-day, game-phase. Is role already in player_features? Add session-clock bucket, anchor-minute bucket for intra-game drift.
3. **Lesson-plan policy.** Given archetype vector and cohort output, how does lesson selection condition on it? Options: (i) fixed prompt templates keyed to nearest-archetype-centroid; (ii) learned policy over (archetype × cohort-split) → lesson variant.
4. **A/B harness.** Lesson variant id → impression → later outcome (KDA delta, winrate on same champ/role in next N games). Where does this storage live? Site analytics DB.
5. **Ethics/UX.** Archetypes stay internal — never shown to user as a label. Avoid "you are a Late-Ganking Jungler" framing; instead surface behaviour ("your first gank averages 5:30 vs cohort 3:45").

Deliverable of this bead: design doc under `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-archetype-lesson-personalization-design.md` with chosen representation, lesson-plan integration, and A/B plan. Implementation plan + tasks follow as separate beads.

**Non-goals:** actual clustering code, any retrieval modification, any UI.

title: M5 follow-up: lesson content from cohort/target decision diff
description:
MVP (beads 9b01bf83-b8e) surfaces the anchor minute + cohort stats but stops short of the actual teaching content. The next slice needs to answer "what separated the cohort winners from losers at the anchor".

Approach:
- At each picked anchor, pull the decoder head outputs (next_decision, next_event, next_frame) for the target player vs the cohort-majority.
- Compare target-game participant decisions in the window [anchor, anchor+60s] vs the aggregated cohort distribution on the winning side.
- Emit lesson text: "at minute M, most winners in your cohort {decision}; you {decision'}".

Dependencies:
- Plan B decoder heads (already landed).
- May need a tiny per-anchor decision-from-tokens extractor (reuse decisions.py where possible).

title: M4 follow-up: inverted per-minute entropy curve
description:
In the M4 eval report (docs/m4_retrieval_eval_report_2026-04-17.md) the per-minute mean cohort outcome entropy at k=64 on both holdouts is highest near minute 10 and drops monotonically toward minute 25:

game_cold:   min10=0.817 -> min25=0.623
player_cold: min10=0.858 -> min25=0.600

This is the inverse of the expected "mid-game is most uncertain" shape. Plan self-review flagged this as a follow-up.

Hypotheses to check:
- model has learned late-game is more discriminable than early-game (plausible: more tempo signals accumulated by min 20+, draft-to-outcome mapping tighter)
- cohort construction collapses as h_t trajectories converge late-game (possible if model under-uses z_t)
- minute-bucket quantization rounds away a real mid-game peak

Next steps:
- log per-minute n_queries alongside entropy (sample-size effect?)
- compare h_t-only vs z_t-only vs full-key (see howtowin.lol-cow ablation)
- inspect a handful of anchors per bucket to eyeball cohort quality

title: M4 follow-up: FAISS-backed retrieval index for production inference
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

The M4 eval index is PyTorch native brute force (exact, ~1 GB tensor, batched cdist+topk on GPU). Adequate for offline eval (~2k queries against 450k corpus). Inadequate for any online surface that needs sub-second per-query lookup at scale.

Swap to FAISS (`IndexFlatL2` first; `IndexIVFFlat` if quantization noise is acceptable) once M5 or any user-facing surface needs it. Keep the same `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` whitened-key contract so the artifact is interchangeable.

**Why:** isolates the dependency-add from the gating-eval work. Lets us prove the model is good *before* paying the FAISS-install + index-format cost.

**How to apply:** trigger when M5 lesson-generator design surfaces a per-anchor latency budget that brute force can't meet, or when corpus grows past ~5M anchors.

title: M4 follow-up: h_t-only and z_t-only ablation baselines
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run two more kNN retrieval evals against the same held-out queries:
- index over `h_t` alone (512-dim, whitened)
- index over `mu_q(z_t)` alone (32-dim, whitened)

Compare entropy curves to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** tells us which sub-block of the concatenated latent actually carries the retrieval signal. If `h_t`-only matches the headline, the stochastic latent is decorative for retrieval; if `z_t`-only matches, the GRU history is. Either finding informs M5 (teaching surface) and any future RSSM iteration.

**How to apply:** only run if the headline M4 entropy disappoints (<0.7 bits) or sits suspiciously close to a single sub-block's expected ceiling. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the slice.

title: M4 follow-up: player-only baseline kNN
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run the same kNN retrieval eval but with the index built over the Plan B player-stream encoder output only (10× per-participant features, no static, no dynamic). Compare cohort outcome entropy to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** clarifies whether retrieval signal is dominated by "similar lineups + skill" rather than "similar in-game state." If player-only nearly matches the headline, the dynamic latent is redundant for retrieval purposes (a finding worth knowing).

**How to apply:** only run after the headline M4 result lands and only if cohort coherence is ambiguous. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the encoder.

title: Set up git-LFS workflow for Hugging Face model repo
description:
For cases where hf upload / hf sync isn't enough (e.g., frequent weight iterations where git history on weights is useful), set up direct git+LFS push to a Hugging Face model repo.

Steps:
- Install git-lfs (pacman -S git-lfs on Arch, apt on Debian-likes)
- Decide which checkpoints warrant repo-versioned LFS vs plain hf upload (rule of thumb: LFS when diffable, bucket/upload when archival)
- hf repos create nyx-haile/howtowin-plan-b-rssm-v1 --type model
- git clone the HF repo, git lfs install, git lfs track "*.pt" "*.safetensors"
- Commit .gitattributes and a first weight file, push via https with HF_TOKEN
- Document the workflow in docs/ and add to a project script (scripts/upload_checkpoint.py)

Depends on admin-3wd (credential helper) for the git push step not to leak the HF token to ~/.git-credentials plaintext.
